CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why should the flag stick be held high when cheering? (1 mark)
   A. To hide the runners
   B. To block the sun
   C. To make noise
   D. So it does not hit anyone

2. Which part of the foot should touch the ground when sprinting? (1 mark)
   A. The heel
   B. The front part of the foot
   C. The ankle
   D. The side only

3. Why do we warm up before sprinting? (1 mark)
   A. To hide from the starter
   B. To prepare muscles and avoid injury
   C. To tire out the muscles
   D. To make the track smooth

4. At the set position, the hips are (1 mark)
   A. on the ground
   B. behind the line only
   C. a little higher than the shoulders
   D. lower than the knees

5. Which quality do rolls and balances build? (1 mark)
   A. Loud singing
   B. Colour mixing
   C. Reading speed
   D. Balance and coordination

6. How long should you hold a crab balance in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Ten minutes
   B. Three to five counts
   C. Half a second
   D. One hour

7. At the start of the side roll, your arms are (1 mark)
   A. behind your back
   B. on your knees
   C. folded on your chest
   D. stretched above your head

8. In which direction should a side roll travel? (1 mark)
   A. In a straight line along the mat
   B. In a curve off the mat
   C. Backwards over your head
   D. Round and round in place

9. Call and response in a folk song means (1 mark)
   A. a soloist leads and the group answers
   B. a single hum
   C. everyone is silent
   D. two drums only

10. Tempo means (1 mark)
   A. the number of verses
   B. the speed of the music
   C. how loud the music is
   D. the name of the song

11. The mood of a song is (1 mark)
   A. its price
   B. the name of the composer
   C. the feeling it gives
   D. its length in metres

12. Dynamics means (1 mark)
   A. the words
   B. the pitch
   C. how loud or soft the music is
   D. the speed

13. What should you do about distracting things behind the subject? (1 mark)
   A. Photograph them too
   B. Add more
   C. Ignore them always
   D. Remove them or change the angle

14. Before sharing a photograph of others, you should (1 mark)
   A. ask them and an adult
   B. hide it
   C. edit their face
   D. post it at once

15. To make the centre of interest clearer you can (1 mark)
   A. move very far away
   B. add lots of clutter
   C. shake the camera
   D. move closer to the subject

16. Photos on a digital device are kept in its (1 mark)
   A. lens
   B. memory
   C. flash
   D. strap

17. What should you do before playing to prevent spreading germs? (1 mark)
   A. Share the recorder
   B. Chew gum
   C. Wash your hands
   D. Eat sweets

18. Which joint has the mouthpiece? (1 mark)
   A. Foot joint
   B. None
   C. Head joint
   D. Middle joint

19. Music is written on a (1 mark)
   A. wall
   B. table
   C. ruler
   D. staff

20. How should you hold the recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Pointing at your face
   B. Pointing down and away from your body at an angle
   C. Above your head
   D. Flat on your lap

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give three warm-up activities before sprinting. (3 marks)

22. Why does a recorder squeak when you blow too hard? (2 marks)

23. What is the centre of interest in a photograph? (3 marks)

24. Describe how to do the side roll safely. (4 marks)

25. Give three ways of storing and handling a recorder safely. (3 marks)

26. Name three types of Kenyan folk songs and say when each is sung. (3 marks)

27. Explain how working in pairs helps when learning the crab balance. (3 marks)

28. State the three commands at the start of a sprint race in order. (2 marks)

29. Describe the steps of taking a photograph with a digital device. (5 marks)

30. Why is light important in photography? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — So it does not hit anyone
   Keeping it high and away from the track avoids hitting people.

2. B — The front part of the foot
   Sprinters land on the balls of the feet.

3. B — To prepare muscles and avoid injury
   Warm muscles work better and are less likely to be hurt.

4. C — a little higher than the shoulders
   On set the hips lift slightly above the shoulders.

5. D — Balance and coordination
   Gymnastics teaches the body to stay steady and move parts together.

6. B — Three to five counts
   Hold the balance for three to five slow counts.

7. D — stretched above your head
   Arms overhead with palms together keep the body long.

8. A — In a straight line along the mat
   Rolling in a straight line keeps you on the mat.

9. A — a soloist leads and the group answers
   The soloist calls and the chorus answers.

10. B — the speed of the music
   Tempo is how fast or slow.

11. C — the feeling it gives
   Mood is the feeling of a song, such as joy or calm.

12. C — how loud or soft the music is
   Dynamics are the loud and soft parts.

13. D — Remove them or change the angle
   A plain background keeps attention on the subject.

14. A — ask them and an adult
   Respect and safety come first.

15. D — move closer to the subject
   Getting closer helps the subject fill the picture.

16. B — memory
   Digital photos are stored in memory.

17. C — Wash your hands
   Clean hands help hygiene.

18. C — Head joint
   The mouthpiece is at the top of the head joint.

19. D — staff
   The staff has five lines and four spaces.

20. B — Pointing down and away from your body at an angle
   The recorder is held pointing down at about 45 degrees.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Jogging, arm circles, leg swings, gentle stretching, short easy strides. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each activity.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: The air is blown too strongly, so the note jumps to a very high shrill sound. Blow more gently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: The main subject that you want the viewer to notice first, for example a friend's face or a flower.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for main subject, 1 mark for noticed first, 1 mark for an example.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Lie on the back with body straight. Stretch the arms overhead with palms together and legs together. Tighten the tummy and point the toes. Roll over on to the side and tummy in a straight line. Get up slowly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep it in a bag or case; keep away from heat; do not drop it; twist joints gently; do not bite it. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Work songs during work, funeral songs when someone dies, naming songs when a baby is named, initiation songs at initiation, marriage songs at weddings, worship songs at worship. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each type with its occasion.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: One learner performs while the other watches and checks, gives feedback, and helps if needed. They swap places.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: On your marks, set, go.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for all three, 1 mark for the correct order.

29. (5 marks)
   Answer: Check the battery and memory and wipe the lens. Decide the subject. Check the light and centre of interest. Hold with two hands and keep elbows close. Frame the subject and press the button gently. Check the result and retake if needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid stage.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Light lets the camera record the picture. With good light the subject is clear.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
